title: Pappardelle with meat sauce

items: 1 medium carrot, peeled and finely chopped
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
1 oz parmesan, shaved with a peeler (about ½ cup)
¼ cup fresh basil leaves, torn

steps: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and carrot and cook 8–10 min, breaking up the meat, until browned with no pink left (160°F) and the vegetables are soft.
Spoon off extra fat. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 min, until the paste darkens slightly.
Add the tomatoes, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat to low, partly cover and simmer at least 30 min, stirring now and then, until thick.
About 15 min before the sauce is done, bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 Tbsp salt. Cook the pappardelle until al dente. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Stir the milk into the sauce and simmer 2 min. Taste and add salt if needed.
Add the pappardelle and a splash of pasta water to the sauce and toss gently with tongs until coated.
Top with shaved parmesan and basil.
tips: For a richer sauce, simmer it up to 1½ hr on low. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Use half ground beef and half ground pork for a softer, richer sauce; cook it to 160°F the same way.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze the sauce alone up to 3 months. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water until it reaches 165°F.
